subject: MSA + Order Form: product use / training carveouts — procurement redlines
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@dataworks.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@dataworks.com, legal@dataworks.com
Date: 2027-09-12 09:14 AM -0700
Subject: Draft order form + redlines (training & output)

Hi Olga — attaching our next pass on the MSA + order form. High level: procurement needs explicit assignment language for outputs used in our product, and Legal wants clarity on training — they’re asking for a carveout that prohibits vendor-side training on any customer content unless we opt in per-product.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm whether Redwood is willing to grant an assignment of customer-generated outputs for productization (we flagged: exclusive? non-exclusive?).
- If assignment is not acceptable, can Redwood offer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, transferable license limited to productization?
- We also want a defined telemetry/feedback license so our engineering team can use anonymized feedback for improving models internally.

We included inline redlines in DW_redlines_v3.docx. Procurement is on a 2-week cadence; would appreciate a quick runbook for how you want to engage (legal vs sales vs engineering).

Thanks,
Sophie Turner
Sr. Contracts Manager | DataWorks Inc.
Attachments: DataWorks_Draft_OrderForm_v3.pdf, DW_redlines_v3.docx
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@dataworks.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-12 10:02 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form + redlines (training & output)

Hi Sophie — thanks for the file and the clear asks. Looping in Ben (account lead) and Marissa (legal) to align on commercial / redline posture. Quick notes from my side for DataWorks to consider:

1) Output ownership vs license
- Redwood position (summary): we generally do not assign title of model-generated outputs to vendors because customers may submit third-party content. Our standard compromise is a broad, perpetual, royalty-free, transferable license to use outputs for productization.
- We can make the license grant explicit for your use-case (customer productization) and scope it to exclude any content where you have third-party obligations.

2) Training / feedback
- We require an explicit opt-in for model retraining on customer data. For customers who opt-out, we will enforce non-training by contract and runtime controls.
- For telemetry / feedback used for quality improvements, we can offer an anonymized feedback license limited to internal model tooling, not for creating derivative models for third-party use.

3) Practical engineering guardrails
- If you accept the non-training default, we’ll add a flag on the account to prevent long-term KV cache ingestion and dataset export. If you opt-in, we’ll provide scope and retention limits.

Next steps from Redwood: Marissa will propose specific language for the license/assignment buckets and a compromise clause that gives DataWorks productization rights while protecting third-party content and Redwood’s ability to operate/patch models. Ben — can you confirm commercial constraints (settlement on assignment vs license)?

Olga
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@dataworks.com>, legal@dataworks.com
Date: 2027-09-13 09:08 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form + redlines (training & output)

Sophie / team —

I reviewed DW_redlines_v3.docx and sketched three options in the attached evidence-scope.xlsx to expedite procurement:

A) Assignment-lite (preferred by DataWorks): customer obtains assignment of outputs. Redwood gives assignment only where outputs do not contain third-party rights. This requires strong representations from DataWorks (they must warrant rights to assign).

B) Perpetual non-exclusive license (Redwood preferred): Redwood grants a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, transferable license to use outputs for internal productization and customer-facing features. Explicitly carve out training and resale.

C) Hybrid: limited assignment for specific deliverables defined in the order form (e.g., customer-provided prompt library & resulting generated assets) + general license for runtime outputs.

Suggested redline language (high level, paste-ready):
"Customer shall have a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free, transferable license to exploit Outputs generated solely from Customer Content for the purposes set forth in the Order Form, provided that Customer represents and warrants that Customer Content does not infringe third-party rights. Except as expressly set forth herein, Redwood retains all rights in the Models and Model Improvements."

On training: insert an opt-in checkbox in the order form that authorizes Redwood to use Customer Content for model training, subject to a mutually-agreed data-use schedule and retention caps. If DataWorks declines the opt-in, we will include an operational guarantee and audit clause to show dataset non-ingestion.

Operational note for Engineering (Olga): to meet procurement timelines we'll need a short runbook describing:
- how opt-in is toggled,
- the retention window,
- proof artifacts for non-ingestion (logs / snapshot).

Will draft the exact contract snippets by EOD and post in the HubSpot deal link.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: evidence-scope.xlsx
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@dataworks.com>, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-13 11:21 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form + redlines (training & output)

Sophie — appreciate the fast turnaround. Commercially, DataWorks is asking for a strong posture on assignment which could shift price / support terms. Two quick options for us to present to leadership:
- Accept the hybrid approach (C) with a modest increase to the reserved capacity commitment to cover risk.
- Keep (B) license-first approach and offer a narrower SLA credit if they need assignment-like guarantees.

Can you indicate which of those routes procurement favors? My team can prepare a short commercial amendment to reflect either path.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@dataworks.com>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-14 04:03 PM -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form + redlines (training & output) — action items and runbook

Team — summary and next actions to keep procurement to their 2-week rhythm: 

1) Marissa to post redline snippets (license + opt-in checkbox + audit language) in HubSpot by EOD 9/14.
2) Ben to prepare two commercial scenarios for leadership review: hybrid (C) with increased reserved capacity commitment vs license-first (B) + SLA credit. Target: decision by 9/20.
3) Engineering runbook (Olga): short doc outlining opt-in toggle, retention caps (default 90 days for telemetry), and audit evidence (log snapshot + policy statement). I will draft the runbook and attach a runtime control checklist to the deal.

Sophie — will that cadence work on your side? If DataWorks confirms a preference between (B) and (C) by 9/16, we’ll have final language and commercial terms ready for procurement review.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
